criterion: RELEASE-PLAN.md N3, open items after criteria 1 to 4: frame timing on Vulkan and HDR10 through a Vulkan swapchain. Neither is a numbered N3 criterion; both carry N2's criteria 3 and 4 over to the Vulkan backend so the Linux and Steam Deck route has the same checks as the Windows route.
written: 2026-10-16, before the code below exists and before any run
change: The Vulkan swapchain reports the output's refresh rate, which the pacing bound needs (it reads intervals against the refresh period T). Windows: the display configuration's exact rational for the monitor holding the window, the same function the D3D12 swapchain uses, moved to one shared header. Linux: VK_GOOGLE_display_timing's refresh cycle when the device offers the extension, otherwise 0 (unknown). The run record gains refresh_hz so the value can be checked without the pacing window.

t1_refresh_windows.what: raw_native_present_vk run --hidden --frames 10 on SwiftShader (Win32 surface) and raw_native_present run --hidden --frames 10 on WARP, on this machine's monitor; hidden windows, nothing covers the screen
t1_refresh_windows.bound: refresh_hz on Vulkan equals refresh_hz on D3D12 exactly (same function, same monitor)

t2_refresh_linux_ci.what: raw_native_present_vk run on lavapipe, X11 on Xvfb and Wayland on headless Weston, in the vulkan-linux CI job
t2_refresh_linux_ci.bound: none; recorded. A value of 0 means the driver does not offer VK_GOOGLE_display_timing on that surface
t2_refresh_linux_ci.prediction: 0 on both (lavapipe's window-system layers are not expected to offer display timing on Xvfb or headless Weston)

t3_rtx_vulkan_queued.what: on the RTX 4090 with RAW_NATIVE_VK_HW=1, under the GPU lock and only after the author agrees to a fullscreen window on the monitor: (a) pacing, 10,000 frames, FIFO, borderless fullscreen, no read-back; (b) 600 presented frames twice and offscreen; (c) hdr, HDR10 (A2B10G10R10, HDR10_ST2084) through the Vulkan swapchain, read back before present
t3_rtx_vulkan_queued.bound: (a) the N2 bound unchanged (evidence/n2-presentation-bounds.json c4): median within 1% of T, p99 at most 1.25 T, at most 0.2% of intervals above 1.5 T; (b) 600 of 600 equal across the three lists and equal to the D3D12 WARP offscreen list; (c) within one 10-bit code of the C++ PQ encode with the wrong-exponent control outside, as N2 criterion 3
t3_rtx_vulkan_queued.prediction: (a) holds, as D3D12 did (median 16.663 ms at 60 Hz); (b) holds; (c) holds if the driver offers HDR10_ST2084 on the surface, which NVIDIA's Windows driver is expected to do whether or not Windows HDR is on; if it does not, the run records the offered colour spaces and the check stays open
t3_rtx_vulkan_queued.status: not run: needs the GPU lock and the author's agreement to a fullscreen test on the machine in use. The job script is prepared in mission-control and not launched.

does_not_prove: Pacing or HDR on a Steam Deck or on RADV; what the panel shows; anything from a software driver beyond the refresh value it reports.

addendum_a.written: 2026-10-16, after the code and before any run
addendum_a.what_changed: The bounds said the Windows refresh function would move to one shared header used by both backends. The layer rules (scripts/check_layers.py) forbid a backend from including a platform file, so the function lives in the Win32 window (raw/platform/window.hpp gains Window::refreshHz) and the D3D12 swapchain keeps its own copy, unchanged. The host takes the swapchain's value when it is non-zero and the window's otherwise, and records which (refresh_source). The Wayland window also reports its output's current mode refresh (wl_output.mode), which the bounds did not plan.
addendum_a.t1_unchanged: t1 still compares the two values on one monitor; it now also checks that the two copies of the function agree.
addendum_a.t2_prediction_revised: X11 on Xvfb: 0, source none. Wayland on headless Weston: Weston's nominal output refresh from wl_output.mode (source window), expected 60 Hz; the value is recorded, not gated.
